analyst.summary: SAMIL's FY26 print (revenue Rs 1,26,104cr +10.94%, PAT Rs 3,859.97cr +1.49%) masks a sharp intra-year swing verified off our internal PIT quarterly data: Q1 FY26 net profit fell 45% YoY (OPM to an 8% five-year low) before a V-shaped recovery to a record Q4 FY26 (revenue Rs 34,309cr, PAT +46% YoY, OPM 11%). The balance sheet is clean (net debt/EBITDA an all-time-low 0.8x) and diversification into consumer electronics (now EBITDA-positive) and aerospace ($1.6bn order book, +20% YoY) is real. But management has made growth explicitly 75%-acquisition-dependent to hit its own $108bn-by-2030 target, and is right now running four concurrent, un-closed-or-just-closed integrations (Nexans, Yutaka/Shinnichi, MTSL buyout, HR Dhauliganga), two of which have already slipped timelines -- a live, current integration-bandwidth signal. At ~39x trailing earnings/3.9x book for a 10% ROE, ~3% net-margin business, plus a proposed 12.5% US tariff pressing on an already-thin 5.5% net margin at the India wiring-harness unit, the multiple leaves little room for error. Net: Hold -- no red flag to sell a well-financed, actively diversifying compounder, but valuation and M&A-execution risk argue against adding.
